parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no documented facility ban, no police targeting of gender-nonconforming people, and no enforcement record at all — the statute is new (Sept 2025), so its silence reflects recency, not a dead letter. What is documented is a fresh, unanimously passed criminalisation with 2–5 year terms, an explicit ministerial statement that foreign violators will be deported, a 'promotion' clause potentially reaching phone/online content, and no functioning recourse: no SOGI anti-discrimination, no mechanism for anti-LGBT violence, military rule with civil society under attack, and only pre-law societal discrimination on record. For a trans visitor these bite through discretion at the border and through a partner being read as same-sex. Absent any trans-specific targeting or evidence the law is used as a lever against gender-nonconforming travellers, this sits in the elevated band rather than high risk — a step above jurisdictions with documented raids, extortion or birth-sex facility rules, but well below any tolerance-with-remedy tier.
